chapter: Reel IV retellings and New York pianists
title: Caruso's champagne Sundays and Mrs. Anderson at the Inn
summary: Caruso comes on Sunday afternoons and gives $200 to divide, and the owner asks the band to play for ignoring patrons.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: That great tenor was down there. The tenor singer. Caruso. He used to come in this restaurant too?

Yeah. he used to come in there on Sunday afternoons, see, when he was in Boston. He'd come down there in the afternoons, and we'd drink champagne, and when he got through, he'd give us $200, to divide this among the group.

We used to make good money--if we didn't make $35 a night, nearly every night-- if people didn't give us any money, we'd go by the bar and hang out at the bar, and Mrs. Anderson would say--that's the lady owned it--she would come out and say, "oh, Mr. Whaley, would you please give us some music?" And I'd say, "Well, these people aint interested in--they're only interested in their own selves. They don't want our music." But I said, "Well, all right. We'll do it. We'll accommodate you." We'd go back there--shucks. Somebody'd start giving us some money. You see 2s, threes, $5.
